rules.content_invariant: Each file imports one or more mathematical modules and runs `#print axioms` on specific theorems from those imports. No `def`, `theorem`, `lemma`, `structure`, or other declaration introducing mathematical content appears in any of these files. Their removal loses zero searchable formal mathematics.

rules.rationale: These files contain no formal mathematical declarations, definitions, theorems, or proofs. They consist solely of `#print axioms` commands that query the Lean kernel for axiom dependencies of theorems defined in other files. They are meta-level build verification scripts, not mathematical content.

summary: Inspected 25 representative files across Foundations and Sharpness directories. The vast majority (175/180 files) contain substantial formal mathematical content: definitions, theorems, lemmas, and proofs in statistical mechanics, ergodic theory, percolation, and related areas. Five files in Foundations (CheckEqualFiberHall.lean, CheckFiniteBidegreeHall.lean, CheckFractionalHall.lean, CheckTailSpecification.lean, CheckWeightedFiniteInjection.lean) contain only `#print axioms` commands - they are meta-level build-time checks that import other files and print which axioms those imports depend on. They contribute no definitions, statements, or proofs of their own.
